title: Spaghetti al pomodoro
description: The simplest Italian pasta: tomatoes cooked down with garlic and olive oil until sweet and thick. The base for many other pasta sauces.

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water with {1 tsp} of the salt to the boil. Slice the garlic thinly.
steps.tip: The water should taste lightly salty. It is the only chance to season the pasta itself.

steps.text: Put {3 tbsp} of the olive oil and the garlic in a cold frying pan, then warm it on medium-low for 3 minutes until the garlic is pale gold.
steps.tip: Starting in a cold pan stops the garlic burning. Brown garlic tastes bitter.

steps.text: Add the tomatoes, basil, a pinch of chili if you like and the rest of the salt. Crush the tomatoes with a spoon and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
steps.tip: It is ready when it is thick and little pools of orange oil appear at the edges.

steps.text: Meanwhile cook the spaghetti until al dente, a little less than the packet says.
steps.tip: Keep a mug of the pasta water before you drain it.

steps: Drain the spaghetti and add it to the sauce with a splash of the pasta water. Toss over the heat for 1 minute until every strand is coated.

steps.text: Serve with grated parmesan and the last of the olive oil drizzled over.
steps.tip: This is the base for many pastas: add tuna, olives and capers, or more chili, and you have another dish.

title: Pasta puttanesca
description: A bold Neapolitan tomato sauce with olives, capers, anchovies and chili, made from what is in the cupboard.
steps: Bring a large pot of water with the salt to the boil. Chop the garlic, anchovies and parsley and halve the olives.

steps.text: Put the olive oil, garlic, chili and anchovies in a cold frying pan and warm on medium-low for 3 minutes, stirring, until the anchovies melt into the oil.
steps.tip: The anchovies dissolve and give a deep, savoury taste, not a fishy one.

steps.text: Add the tomatoes, olives and capers, crush the tomatoes with a spoon and simmer for 12 minutes until thick.
steps.tip: Taste before adding any salt: olives, capers and anchovies are all salty.

steps.text: Meanwhile cook the pasta until al dente, a little less than the packet says.
steps.tip: Keep a mug of the pasta water before you drain it.

steps.text: Drain the pasta and toss it with the sauce, a splash of pasta water and the parsley. Serve straight away.
steps.tip: Puttanesca is traditionally eaten without parmesan.

title: Creamy mushroom pasta
description: Golden fried mushrooms in a garlicky cream and parmesan sauce. Ready in 30 minutes.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Slice the mushrooms and chop the onion, garlic and parsley.

steps.text: Heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan on high. Add the mushrooms in one layer and fry for 8 minutes, stirring only now and then, until golden and their juice has cooked away.
steps.tip: Do not salt the mushrooms yet, or they let out water and stew instead of browning.

steps: Turn the heat to medium, add the onion for 4 minutes until soft, then the garlic for a few seconds.

steps.text: Meanwhile cook the pasta until al dente, a little less than the packet says.
steps.tip: Keep a mug of the pasta water before you drain it.

steps: Pour the cream into the mushrooms, add half the parmesan, a pinch of salt and the pepper and let it bubble for 2 minutes. Toss in the drained pasta with a splash of pasta water.

steps.text: Serve with the rest of the parmesan and the parsley.
steps.tip: To make it heartier, add diced ham or leftover chicken with the cream.

title: Pasta with broccoli, garlic and chili
description: Broccoli cooked in the pasta pot, then crushed into garlic and chili oil so it becomes a green sauce. Cheap, quick and healthy.
steps: Bring a large pot of water with the salt to the boil. Cut the broccoli into small florets, peel the stalk and slice it thinly. Slice the garlic.

steps.text: Add the pasta to the boiling water. When it has 5 minutes left on the packet, add the broccoli to the same pot.
steps.tip: Cooking them together saves a pot, and the broccoli water flavours the pasta.

steps.text: Meanwhile put the olive oil, garlic, chili and anchovies (if using) in a cold frying pan and warm on low for 4 minutes until the garlic is pale gold.
steps.tip: Leave out the anchovies to keep it vegetarian.

steps.text: Keep a mug of the pasta water, drain, and tip the pasta and broccoli into the garlic oil. Toss for 2 minutes on medium heat, crushing some of the broccoli with your spoon.
steps.tip: The crushed broccoli turns into a green sauce that coats the pasta. Add pasta water if it looks dry.

steps: Grate in a little lemon zest, squeeze in the juice, add most of the parmesan and toss. Serve with the rest of the parmesan on top.

title: Creamy salmon and spinach pasta
description: Pieces of salmon and wilted spinach in a light lemon and dill cream sauce. A quick way to get fish on the table.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Take the skin off the salmon, cut it into 2 cm cubes and season with a pinch of the salt. Chop the garlic.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a large frying pan on medium-high and cook the salmon for 3 minutes, turning gently, until just opaque. Lift it out.
steps.tip: Take it out a little underdone: it finishes cooking in the sauce.

steps: Add the garlic for a few seconds, then the cream, dill and a little grated lemon zest. Let it bubble for 2 minutes, then stir in the spinach until it wilts.

steps.text: Meanwhile cook the pasta until al dente, a little less than the packet says.
steps.tip: Keep a mug of the pasta water before you drain it.

steps: Toss the drained pasta into the sauce with a splash of pasta water. Fold the salmon back in gently and squeeze over the lemon juice.

steps.text: Serve with black pepper on top.
steps.tip: Smoked salmon works too: stir it in at the end, off the heat.

title: Pasta with sausage and peppers
description: Browned smoked sausage, sweet peppers and onion in a paprika tomato sauce. Hearty and quick.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Slice the sausages into rounds and the peppers and onion into strips. Chop the garlic.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan on medium-high and brown the sausages for 5 minutes.
steps.tip: Smoked sausage (kobasica) from the deli counter works well.

steps: Add the peppers and onion and fry for 8 minutes until soft and a little charred. Stir in the garlic and paprika for a few seconds.
Pour in the passata and simmer for 10 minutes while you cook the pasta until al dente.

steps.text: Toss the drained pasta into the sauce with a splash of pasta water and serve with grated parmesan.
steps.tip: Taste before salting: the sausage is already salty.

title: Pasta with peas and bacon
description: Short pasta with sweet peas, crisp bacon, butter and parmesan. A 20-minute family favourite in Italy and Croatia.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. Dice the bacon and chop the onion finely.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan on medium and fry the bacon and onion for 6 minutes until the bacon is golden.

steps.text: Add the peas and a splash of water, cover and cook for 5 minutes until tender.
steps.tip: Crush a few peas with a fork: they make the sauce creamy.

steps.text: Meanwhile cook the pasta until al dente.
steps.tip: Keep a mug of the pasta water before you drain it.

steps: Toss the drained pasta into the peas with the butter, most of the parmesan, the pepper and a splash of pasta water until glossy. Serve with the rest of the parmesan.

title: Baked macaroni cheese
description: Pasta in a rich cheese sauce, baked under a crisp, golden crumb. Comfort food children love.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Bring a pot of salted water to the boil and cook the pasta 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain.
steps.tip: It finishes cooking in the oven, so it must still be firm.

steps.text: Make the cheese sauce: melt the butter in a pot on medium, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk a little at a time. Simmer for 5 minutes, whisking, until thick.
steps.tip: Adding the milk slowly while whisking keeps it smooth.

steps: Take it off the heat and stir in most of the cheddar, the mustard, nutmeg and a pinch of salt until melted.
Mix the pasta with the sauce, tip it into a baking dish and scatter the rest of the cheddar, the parmesan and the breadcrumbs over the top.

steps.text: Bake for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.
steps.tip: Stir broccoli florets or diced ham into the pasta before baking for a complete meal.

title: Đuveč with chicken
description: Rice baked with peppers, zucchini, tomato and paprika under browned chicken legs. A one-pot Sunday dish from across the Balkans.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Chop the onions, peppers, zucchini and carrot into small cubes. Rinse the rice. Season the chicken with half the salt and a little of the paprika.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide ovenproof pot on medium-high and brown the chicken for 8 minutes, skin side first, until golden. Set it aside.
steps.tip: No ovenproof pot? Brown in a pan, then move everything to a deep baking dish.

steps: Fry the onion, pepper and carrot in the same pot for 8 minutes, then the zucchini for 2 minutes. Stir in the tomato paste and the rest of the paprika for a few seconds.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, the crumbled stock cube, the rest of the salt and {700 ml} hot water and bring to the boil.

steps.text: Lay the chicken on top, skin side up. Cover with a lid or foil and bake for 40 minutes, then uncover and bake for 15 minutes more until the skin is crisp.
steps.tip: If the rice looks dry before it is soft, add a splash of hot water.

steps.text: Scatter with parsley and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.
steps.tip: Đuveč is even better reheated the next day. It keeps 3 days.

title: Prawn fried rice
description: Day-old rice fried hot with prawns, egg, peas and carrot, seasoned with soy, ginger and sesame.
ahead: cook the rice and chill it

steps.text: Cook the rice the day before and keep it in the fridge. Dice the carrot, slice the spring onion, grate the garlic and ginger and beat the eggs. Thaw frozen prawns and pat them dry.
steps.tip: Cold rice fries into separate grains. Fresh rice turns sticky.

steps: Heat {1 tbsp} of the sunflower oil in a wok or large frying pan on high. Fry the prawns for 2 minutes until pink, then lift them out.
Add the rest of the oil, the carrot, garlic and ginger and stir-fry for 2 minutes, then the peas for 1 minute.
Push everything to one side, scramble the eggs in the space until just set, then mix them in.

steps.text: Add the rice, breaking up lumps, and stir-fry for 4 minutes, pressing it against the hot pan.
steps.tip: Keep the heat high and spread the rice out so it fries rather than steams.

steps: Add the soy sauce, sesame oil, prawns and spring onion and toss for 1 minute until hot. Serve straight away.

title: Risi e bisi (rice and peas)
description: The Venetian spring dish: creamy rice with lots of peas, a little pancetta and parmesan, loose enough to eat with a spoon.

steps.text: Crumble the stock cubes into {1300 ml} hot water and keep it warm on low heat. Chop the onion, bacon and parsley.
steps.tip: Hot stock keeps the rice cooking evenly.

steps: Melt half the butter in a wide pan on medium and fry the onion and bacon for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains look a little see-through at the edges.

steps.text: Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: Wait until each ladle is almost absorbed before adding the next.

steps.text: Add the peas and two more ladles of stock and cook for 5 minutes until the rice is soft.
steps.tip: Risi e bisi should be looser than risotto, almost a thick soup.

steps: Take the pan off the heat, stir in the rest of the butter, the parmesan and parsley, cover and rest for 2 minutes before serving.
